title: Lior and the Garden
premise: Lior Dravenmoor, youngest smuggler of the fading Thornfell Guild, has always kept to the hidden roads and never asked what his clients carry. When the crown declares a hunt for the gifted, his newest cargo turns out to be a boy whose soul was sold to the court beneath the mountain — and the Guild's own master brokered the sale to buy the guild's survival. Lior must choose between loyalty to the family that raised him and the truth of what they've become, leading a ragtag found family of hunted gift-bearers down into the mountain court to steal the boy's soul back before the long winter seals the passes. He succeeds, but at the cost of exposing the Guild's betrayal, and the guild dies so that something kinder can be born from its ashes.
about_author: Gideon Nystrom is the pen name of a former trail guide who spent a decade leading expeditions through remote mountain passes before turning to fantasy. His fiction is known for its tactile landscapes, morally tangled loyalties, and quiet characters who do brave things badly.

chapters.title: The Last Fair Cargo
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Guiding a sealed crate through the Thornfell passes, Lior discovers it holds a living boy whose soul-scent marks him as gifted — and as crown property. The Guild's master, Vess, orders the delivery completed to protect the guild from the king's new hunt. Lior hesitates, then obeys, but the boy's whispered plea follows him home. Emotional beat: uneasy complicity; the first crack in Lior's loyalty.

chapters.title: What the Guild Sold
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, with an interlude from the boy, Tam, in the mountain court. Lior digs into the guild's ledgers and finds the sale was no bargain — Vess traded Tam's soul for the crown's silence about the guild's other gifted members. When crown hunters burn a waystation and kill a guildsman, Lior gathers the survivors: a disgraced hedge-witch, a mute tracker, and Tam's sister. Emotional beat: betrayal hardening into resolve; a found family begins to form.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Alternating Lior and hedge-witch Sera's POV. The party descends through smugglers' roads into the mountain court, where souls are kept as currency and winter is a wall the court itself maintains. They bargain, bluff, and finally fight their way to Tam's soul-vessel, but Vess arrives — sent to ensure the sale holds — and Lior must face the woman who raised him. Emotional beat: climax; loyalty and truth collide in open confrontation as the winter seals the exits.

chapters.title: After the Long Winter
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior shatters the vessel and returns Tam's soul, collapsing the court's hold on the mountain's winter; the passes open, and the crown's claim dies with the court's broker. Vess, defeated, chooses exile over the guild's old bargains. The survivors bury the guild's ledgers and found a new, honest road-company with Tam and his sister at its heart. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution — the old family dies, a truer one is born.
